what_its_for: Daptomycin is an antibiotic used to treat serious bacterial skin infections and certain bloodstream infections, including those caused by a tough bacteria called MRSA (methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus). It works by attacking and breaking down the outer wall of harmful bacteria, killing them.
how_to_take: Daptomycin is given as an injection directly into your vein (IV infusion) by a nurse or healthcare provider, either in a hospital, clinic, or sometimes at home with a home health nurse. You should NOT take this medicine by mouth. Each infusion usually takes about 30 minutes. Try to receive your infusion at the same time each day. Do not stop treatment early, even if you feel better, unless your doctor tells you to.
dosing: Your doctor will decide your dose based on your weight, the type of infection you have, and how well your kidneys are working. The usual dose is given once every 24 hours. Your healthcare team will prepare and administer the correct dose for you. Never adjust your dose on your own.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, contact your doctor or home health nurse right away. Try to receive the missed dose as soon as possible, but if your next scheduled dose is less than 8 hours away, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Never receive two doses at once to make up for a missed one.
storage: If you are receiving daptomycin at home, store unmixed vials in the refrigerator between 36°F and 46°F (2°C to 8°C). Keep it in the original packaging and protect it from light. Do not freeze. Once the medication is mixed (reconstituted), it should be used within 12 hours if kept at room temperature, or within 48 hours if kept in the refrigerator. Keep all medications out of reach of children and pets. Do not pour leftover medication down the drain — ask your pharmacist how to safely dispose of it.
what_to_avoid: Avoid taking cholesterol-lowering medications called statins (such as atorvastatin, simvastatin, or rosuvastatin) while using daptomycin without talking to your doctor first, as this combination can increase the risk of muscle problems. Avoid strenuous physical activity or heavy exercise if you develop muscle pain, weakness, or tenderness. Do not use daptomycin to treat lung (pneumonia) infections, as it does not work well in lung tissue. Tell your doctor about all medications, vitamins, and supplements you take.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor or seek emergency care right away if you experience: sudden muscle pain, tenderness, weakness, or cramping (especially if accompanied by dark-colored urine, which could signal a serious muscle condition called rhabdomyolysis); numbness, tingling, or burning in your hands or feet; severe diarrhea that is watery or bloody (may occur weeks after treatment); signs of an allergic reaction such as rash, hives, swelling of your face, lips, or throat, or difficulty breathing; chest pain or trouble breathing (could signal a rare lung reaction); yellowing of your skin or eyes, or dark urine (signs of liver problems); signs of a new infection or fever that gets worse or does not improve after a few days of treatment.
when_it_works: You may start to feel better within a few days of starting daptomycin, but it is very important to complete the full course of treatment as prescribed by your doctor, which is usually 7 to 14 days or longer depending on your infection. Do not stop the medication early just because you feel better — stopping too soon can allow the bacteria to come back and become harder to treat.
special_populations: Kidney problems: If your kidneys do not work well, your doctor may give you a lower dose or change how often you receive the medication. Your kidney function will be monitored regularly during treatment. Elderly patients: Older adults may need dose adjustments based on kidney function. Children: Daptomycin can be used in children aged 1 year and older for certain infections, with doses adjusted by weight and age. Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. Daptomycin should only be used during pregnancy if clearly needed. It may pass into breast milk, so talk to your doctor about the safest option for you and your baby.
